title: First Report of Vibrio harveyi From Starry Flounder (Platichthys stellatus) With Phenotypic, Pathogenicity and Whole‐Genome Characterization
content:
ABSTRACT

Vibrio harveyi is a prominent bacterial pathogen of marine aquaculture. Vibrio harveyi has not previously been reported in starry flounder. In this study, phenotypic and genotypic characterizations and pathogenicity assessments of V. harveyi isolated from starry flounder in South Korea were conducted. Phylogenetic analysis identified strains VH-SF-1, VH-SF-2, VH-SF-4 and VH-SF-5 as V. harveyi . Motility assays showed that VH-SF-2 displayed the highest activity at 27°C. In pathogenicity tests, VH-SF-2 caused 100% mortality within 16 and 48 h at doses of 3 × 108 and 3 × 107 CFU/fish, respectively, whereas a 10% mortality rate was observed at 3 × 106 CFU/fish. The lethal dose (LD50) was estimated to range from 3 × 106 to 3 × 107 CFU/fish, providing the first evidence of the pathogenicity of V. harveyi in starry flounder. These findings suggest that V. harveyi may emerge as a novel pathogen of this species. To investigate genomic characteristics and virulence factors, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was conducted. Strain VH-SF-2 harboured multiple virulence-related mechanisms, including outer membrane proteins, motility, quorum sensing, bacterial secretion systems, iron uptake and regulation and virulence regulators. The study aimed to elucidate the biological and pathogenic characteristics of V. harveyi isolated from starry flounder.
